assumptions: Path-contains checks (/data_reuse/, /cdap_, /adam/, raw/, _anon_, ...) are made on the folder path relative to incoming/, with a '/' added at the start and at the end, so that a first or last folder can still match.
Rules 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 ('a data format') use the slash-style format (/adam/, /sdtm/, raw/). Only rule 4 (ANON) uses the underscore format.
The underscore format follows the same order as the slash format: _adam_, then _sdtm_, then _raw_ or _restricted_raw_.
Moving a file to error/ is also a move: server-side copy, check, then delete the source. If that fails, the file fails and so does the run.
'Confirm the target exists' means a HEAD on the target returns an object of the same size as the source.
The server-side copy keeps the object's metadata. Files moved to error/ keep the tags copied from the source unchanged ('no tag change').
If the delete fails after a successful copy, the target stays in place and the source stays in incoming/. The next run copies it again, overwriting the target.
A file name has an extension when it contains a '.'.
The 'contains _ia' check on the CDAP last folder is case-sensitive.
CDAP interim: if the third part starts with 'ia', that 'ia' is replaced by 'ia_'. Otherwise 'ia_' is put in front of the whole part.
The per-file report goes to the run log.
Runs do not overlap: at most one run is active at a time.
The cron '*/45 * * * *' is used as written (it fires at :00 and :45 of each hour).

questions.text: Are the path-contains checks made on the folder path relative to incoming/, with '/' added at the start and at the end, so a first or last folder can match /adam/ or /data_reuse/?
questions.proposed_assumption: Yes: the checks run on '/' + folder path relative to incoming/ + '/'.

questions.text: For rules 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6, does 'a data format' include the underscore formats (_adam_, ...), or only /adam/, /sdtm/ and raw/?
questions.proposed_assumption: Only the slash-style formats. The underscore formats are used by ANON only.

questions.text: When a folder path contains several underscore formats, which one wins?
questions.proposed_assumption: The same order as the slash format: adam, then sdtm, then raw (including restricted_raw).

questions.text: CDAP interim: what happens when the third '_' part does not start with 'ia' (e.g. cdap_2021_x_ia3)?
questions.proposed_assumption: A leading 'ia' is replaced by 'ia_'. Otherwise 'ia_' is put in front of the whole third part.

questions.text: Is the CDAP 'last folder contains _ia' check case-sensitive?
What does 'confirm the target exists' check?
questions.proposed_assumption: A HEAD on the target succeeds and its size equals the source size.

questions.text: Is the move to error/ also copy, check and delete, so that its failure fails the run?
questions.proposed_assumption: Yes. It is a move like any other and only skips the tag change.

questions.text: Files moved to error/ get 'no tag change'. Should they keep the source's tags?
questions.proposed_assumption: Yes. The copy carries the source's tags and metadata over unchanged.

questions.text: S3 tag values are limited to 256 characters and a restricted character set. What happens to longer paths or paths with other characters?
questions.proposed_assumption: Tagging is attempted with the full path. A rejection is logged as a warning and the file still counts as moved.

questions.text: What happens if the delete fails after a successful copy?
questions.proposed_assumption: The file fails and the run fails. The target stays, and the next run copies the file again (overwriting the target) and retries the delete.

questions.text: Where should the per-file report go?
questions.proposed_assumption: The run log, one line per file: source, target, rule or error reason, status.

questions.text: May runs overlap if one run takes longer than 45 minutes?
questions.proposed_assumption: No: at most one run is active at a time.

questions.text: '*/45 * * * *' fires at :00 and :45 of each hour, not every 45 minutes. Is that intended?
questions.proposed_assumption: Use the cron exactly as written.

questions.text: Does a file name like '.DS_Store' or 'a.' count as having an extension?
questions.proposed_assumption: Any name that contains a '.' counts as having an extension, so the file is processed.
